items.title: ‘Cruise ship’ condo proposal returns with changes in Mississauga
items.summary: A contested condo project, which some described as a “cruise ship,” is back up for consideration in Mississauga. The proposed development at 900 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Lorne Park has come up against resistance from area residents. The property is next to Richard’s Memorial Park, currently home to a single-detached house with a pool. Initially proposed as an 11-storey condo building with 178 units in 2023, the proposal changed to 10 storeys with 188 units in 2025. ” Residents who formed the 900 Lakeshore Committee raised concerns about “hurricane-force winds” caused by the building, a disruption to the Carolinian Forest ecology, increased traffic, parking overspill onto parkland lots and groundwater management. Now, a nine-storey condominium apartment building with 161 dwelling units is proposed and is scheduled to be considered at the Sept. 8 Planning and Development Committee meeting. items.title: What’s Open & Closed Labour Day Mississauga Monday Sept. 7, 2026
items.summary: Labour Day in Mississauga and across Canada falls on Monday, Sept. 7, 2026. The early September holiday originally came about as a way to give workers the chance to campaign for better working conditions and pay. However, these days, it’s part of a long weekend during which you can relax. Here’s what’s open and closed in Mississauga on Labour Day 2026: Enter for an exclusive chance to win 2 tickets to Great Outdoors Comedy Festival (GOCF), a $500 Gift Card to Square One Shopping Centre, and a Visit Mississauga Swag Bag. The approximate retail value of the prize is $1,000.

items.title: City of Mississauga Books 2026 Gen X Comedy Show
items.summary: The show will be held at the Living Arts Centre on October 9 The City of Mississauga and saugaLIVE are enlisting four of the funniest Gen X creators and comedians for a night of laughter, nostalgia and getting older this fall with the GenX Takeover Comedy Tour. , the evening will feature sets from the Real Slim Sherri, Kelly Manno, Dadbod Veteran (Jon Willington), Professor Nick Harrison and Justin Rupple. Tickets are available to purchase now. Upgrade your night with a post-show VIP meet and greet with a photo opt, autographed poster and swag bag. A buffet dinner add-on will also be available before the show at the LIVE Restaurant, which is steps away from the theatre. Reservations are recommended, but walk-ins are also accepted.

items.title: Dog days of summer end with a paw-sitive splash
items.summary: Mississauga dogs invited to make a splash at the annual Dog Swim on September 12. Entertainment and activities | September 1, 2026 As summer winds down, dog owners are invited to treat their furry companions to a swim at the City’s annual Dog Swim on September 12. This popular event gives dogs a chance to splash and play in some of Mississauga’s outdoor pools before they close for the season. The event also supports the Animal Services Special Care for Animals and Resources Fund (SCARF). While the swim is free to attend, donations to SCARF help provide enhanced care for animals in the City’s shelter, including medications, specialized veterinary treatment, foster support and shelter improvements. Since launching in 2019, the Dog Swim has become a popular end-of-summer tradition, bringing together dogs and their owners for a day of swimming, exercise and social time, all while supporting animals in need. To participate, dog owners must register online and complete a mandatory waiver form and follow all Dog Swim Pool Rules. Dogs must be vaccinated as outlined in the City’s rules. The City of Mississauga’s annual Dog Swim gives residents the chance to bring their dogs to enjoy the outdoor pools before they close for the season. Note: People are not permitted in the pool, but may watch their pets from the pool deck.

items.title: Toronto family plans march for 19-year-old killed by police in Mississauga
items.summary: A march is being planned this weekend for a 19-year-old Toronto man who was killed in a police-involved shooting in Mississauga earlier this month. Kaleym Davy was shot and killed following an interaction with Toronto police on Delfi Road in Mississauga on Aug. 6, according to his family. A march in Davy’s memory is now planned for Saturday, Aug. 22, according to a social media post shared by his aunt. , although organizers have not publicly disclosed the location. The family is asking those who want to attend to contact organizers directly for the location. The march comes as Davy’s family continues to call for answers surrounding his death and raises money through a GoFundMe campaign. The fundraiser has a public goal of $45,000, while the family says its overall goal is $100,000. The money will go toward funeral and burial expenses, as well as legal fees and representation as the family considers pursuing legal action. “Our goal is not only to give Kaleym the farewell he deserves, but also to help family find answers and pursue justice,” the GoFundMe says. “Losing a child is something no family should ever have to experience.

items.title: Inquest set for 88-year-old who died after well-being check by Peel police in 2023
items.summary: An inquest will be held next week into the death of an 88-year-old man who died after he fell down a flight of stairs during a well-being check by Peel police in Mississauga nearly three years ago.

items.title: Mississauga Arrest Caps Months-Long Human Trafficking Investigation Into Barrie Escort Service
items.summary: According to INsauga, a 50-year-old Barrie man was arrested in Mississauga on the weekend following a months-long human trafficking investigation. The outlet reports Barrie police began investigating in June after receiving information that the man was allegedly recruiting women to provide sexual services for an escort service run out of his home. INsauga reports investigators subsequently identified online ads for sexual services linked to the suspect and executed a search warrant at an address in Springwater Township on August 12. According to the outlet, Michael Brocklebank was arrested in Mississauga without incident this past Sunday. INsauga reports Brocklebank now faces multiple charges, including trafficking in persons, material benefit from trafficking in persons, advertising sexual services and failing to comply with a probation order.

items.title: Streetsville Village Square Goes to the Dogs for Toronto Dog Mom Day Celebration
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto Dog Moms is hosting Dogsville 2026, its biggest event yet, in Streetsville Village Square on September 26 to celebrate Toronto Dog Mom Day. The outlet reports the free, family-friendly festival will bring together hundreds of dog parents, animal lovers and pet-friendly businesses for an afternoon of vendors, live entertainment, interactive experiences and photo opportunities. INsauga reports Toronto Dog Moms is partnering with Music Day in Canada to bring in a musical lineup that includes Veneice, Gracie Ella, Avery, Neddy and Jennie Law. According to the outlet, organizers describe the event as a chance for pet parents to bond with their dogs, connect with fellow dog lovers and support small businesses. INsauga reports the festival takes place at 213 Queen Street South in Streetsville, with more details available on the event's Eventbrite page.

items.title: Already-Saturated Ground Raises Flood Risk as Storm System Moves Through Mississauga
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a weather system moving through southern Ontario is expected to bring additional rainfall and thunderstorms to the city through Monday afternoon and evening, with a risk of watershed flooding. The city reports the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority and Credit Valley Conservation are advising residents to prepare for changing conditions as the system passes through. According to the city, soils in the area are already saturated and water levels in rivers and streams are already elevated, meaning watercourses could respond quickly to additional rainfall. The city reports the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority expects river and stream levels to keep rising over the following 24 hours, with stronger, faster flows expected through the day and into the next. According to the city, flood messages like this one are issued by conservation authorities specifically to help residents understand changing conditions and take appropriate precautions.

items.title: 7,100-Square-Foot Mississauga Listing Pairs a Butler's Pantry With a Backyard Pool
items.summary: According to INsauga's House of the Week feature, this week's pick is a Mississauga home offering more than 7,100 square feet of living space across three finished levels. The outlet reports the main floor has 10-foot ceilings, solid pine plank flooring and custom millwork, while the kitchen includes granite countertops, Wolf appliances, a Sub-Zero refrigerator and a walk-in wine room. INsauga reports the primary bedroom features a six-piece ensuite and dressing room, and the basement has its own separate entrance leading to a recreation lounge, wet bar, home theatre and a sixth bedroom. According to the outlet, the backyard includes a new pool, hot tub, covered pergola with a wood-burning fireplace and a built-in barbecue. INsauga reports the property sits near Port Credit Village, Clarkson Village, the University of Toronto Mississauga and Trillium Health Partners, with listing details provided by Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. Brokerage.

items.title: Trillium Health Partners' New Etobicoke Hospital Nears Halfway Point on $1.3-Billion Build
items.summary: According to INsauga, the new Gilgan Family Queensway Health Centre in Etobicoke, a $1.3-billion project just steps from Mississauga, is now nearly halfway complete. The outlet reports the hospital is part of the Trillium Health Partners network, which also includes Mississauga Hospital and Credit Valley Hospital, and is scheduled to open in 2029. INsauga reports the new patient tower has been described by hospital officials as a modern nine-storey facility with more than 350 beds and fully private patient rooms designed to improve privacy and infection control. According to the outlet, work on the project began in February 2024 and is being built by Mississauga-based construction firm EllisDon. INsauga reports Trillium Health Partners officials have said the new hospital will increase the network's capacity to provide care from Milton to Toronto as the surrounding communities continue to grow.

items.title: Horse-Drawn Wagon Rides and Reptile Exhibits Headline Erindale Park's Forestry Fall Festival
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, National Forest Week and a slate of fall nature programming will run from September 19 to November 7, highlighting the role trees play in the city's health and resilience. The city says the second annual Forestry Fall Festival returns to Erindale Park with family-friendly activities including horse-drawn wagon rides, reptile and snake exhibits, and opportunities to plant a tree. According to the city, attendees can meet the forestry experts behind Mississauga's urban forest and get an up-close look at the specialized equipment used to maintain it. The city reports the broader programming is meant to let residents connect with nature, learn from forestry experts and discover the benefits of the city's urban forest, from cleaner air to reduced summer heat. According to the city, events throughout the six-week period include guided wildlife walks and free tree giveaways for residents' yards.
